name: Automations
description: Rules that react to what happens in the shop: an order is placed or changes, an enquiry arrives or waits too long — wait if you like, check the conditions, then act: a Telegram message, a webhook you compose yourself, a new status or manager. One rule engine replaces the class of integration modules that only ever POST JSON somewhere: analytics, a chat notification, Make/Zapier, a CRM lead. It also sends verification codes through an SMS gateway or any other HTTP service.

settings.label: Request timeout, seconds
settings.help: How long a webhook may take before it counts as failed. Runs happen in the queue, so this never delays a customer — but a receiver that hangs would hold a worker.

settings.label: Retry an action the receiver did not take, times
settings.help: A webhook whose host could not be reached, a Telegram message the network dropped, a receiver answering "try later" (429) or failing on its side (5xx): that one action — not the rest of the rule — is run again after the interval below, this many times, then marked failed. Every attempt is a row of the run log. 0 — never. A refusal (a wrong token, a chat not found, a 4xx) is never retried: it stays until fixed.

keywords.en: retry attempts resend telegram webhook connection error timeout
keywords.ru: повтор попытки переотправить телеграм вебхук ошибка соединения таймаут

settings.label: Retry after, minutes
settings.help: Between one attempt and the next.

settings.label: Allow requests to private addresses
settings.help: Off by default and should stay off in production: the URL is written by an admin but the request is made by the server, from inside your network. With this off, localhost, link-local (169.254.x — cloud metadata) and private ranges are refused. Turn it on only on a development machine talking to a local receiver.

settings.label: Keep the run log, days
settings.help: Older entries are deleted nightly. The log is what tells you whether the receiver actually got it, so keep enough of it to answer that after a weekend.
